opportunities.name: arXiv topic search → Semantic Scholar citation lookup → log to Notes
opportunities.description: For a research topic and year, search arXiv Advanced Search (title field, subject category, specific year), open the top result, look up its citation count on Semantic Scholar, and add a summary line to Notes.
steps: On arxiv.org click Search, then Advanced search
Type {topic} in the Search term field (Title)
Check the {subject} category box (e.g. Computer Science or Quantitative Biology)
Select 'Specific year' and type {year}
Click Search and open the top result (arXiv ID link)
Copy the paper title and first author
On Semantic Scholar, dismiss the cookie banner if it appears, type the paper title in the search box and press Enter
Open the matching result and read the citation count
In Notes, click 'New note' and enter '{topic} ({year}): {title} by {first author}, {citations} citations', then press Enter

instances.values: topic='retrieval augmented generation', Computer Science, 2023 → RIGHT… by Run-Ze Fan, 11 citations
topic='protein structure diffusion', Quantitative Biology, 2024 → Accelerating Inference in Molecular Diffusion Models… by Ian Dunn, 7 citations
topic='graph neural networks traffic forecasting', Computer Science, 2022 → Efficient Traffic State Forecasting… by Bin Lei, 1 citation

opportunities.name: Case law lookup on CourtListener + related statute on Cornell LII → log to Notes
opportunities.description: For a court case name and a related U.S.C. section, find the case on CourtListener to get its citation and decision date, find the statute's title on Cornell LII, and add a combined note.
steps: On CourtListener open Case Law → Search Case Law
Type {case name} in the keyword search box and press Enter
Open the Supreme Court opinion result and note the U.S. Reports citation and decision date
On Cornell LII, type {statute citation} (e.g. '18 U.S.C. 2703') in the search box and press Enter
Open the matching U.S. Code section result and note its title
In Notes, click 'New note' and enter '{case}: {citation}, decided {date}. See {statute} ({statute title})', then press Enter

instances.values: Carpenter v. United States; 18 U.S.C. 2703 (Required disclosure of customer communications or records)
Bostock v. Clayton County; 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2 (Unlawful employment practices)
Miranda v. Arizona; 18 U.S.C. 3501 (Admissibility of confessions)

opportunities.name: Event planning: Peerspace venue search + 1800flowers flower search + summary email
opportunities.description: For an event type, city and date, search Peerspace for venues, search 1800flowers for flowers, and draft an email summarizing venue, catering and flower options to the organizer.
steps: On Peerspace, clear and type {activity} in 'What are you planning?'
Clear and type {city} in 'Where?' and pick the matching suggestion
Click Search (retry if the activity is not recognized)
On 1800flowers, type {flower query} in the search box and press Enter
Open the chosen product and note its name and price
In Mail, compose a new message to {recipient} with subject '{activity} on {date}: venue, food, flowers'
Write a body with guest count, venue rate, catering minimum and the flower choice and price
Send or discard the draft

instances.values: Team offsite, Chicago (only the venue search was done)
Birthday party, San Francisco; flowers 'tulips' (no email)
Product launch, New York; flowers 'white orchids' → White Phalaenopsis Orchid $59.99; email to priya@example.com, 60 guests, Jan 14
